title: Unrestricted file upload types in documents module
reasoning: The accept attribute is configurable and defaults to document types, but client-side accept is not enforced—it's only a UI hint. Malicious users can bypass this and upload arbitrary files (executables, scripts, etc.) if the backend /api/rag-upload does not validate file types server-side. The feature allows custom accept via opts.accept, which could be misconfigured to allow dangerous MIME types. No client-side validation of file.type occurs before upload.
reproduction: Modify the accept attribute in browser DevTools or use curl to POST a .exe or .js file to uploadEndpoint. If backend does not validate MIME type and file content, arbitrary files are stored in the knowledge base.
recommendation: Add client-side file.type validation before upload as defense-in-depth. Document that backend MUST validate file types and scan for malware. Reject files with dangerous extensions or MIME types. Use allowlist-based validation on backend.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist. No client-side type checking is implemented; reliance is solely on backend (which is outside this module's scope).
suggestedRegressionTest: Unit test: verify upload() rejects files not matching opts.accept MIME types. Integration test: confirm backend rejects .exe, .sh, .js uploads even if client sends them.
minimumFixScope: src/src/portal/modules/documents.tsx upload function (lines 468-487): add client-side file.type validation against accept before sending to backend
